topics.t: Kamarajar Port: second container terminal on the PPP route
topics.news: Kamarajar Port in Tamil Nadu has invited bids for a second container terminal costing about ₹4,288 crore, to be built on a design, build, finance, operate and transfer (DBFOT) basis under public–private partnership with a 40-year concession. The terminal is planned in two phases, of about 1.1 and 0.9 million twenty-foot equivalent units, adding about 2 million units of annual capacity.

rows: Adds capacity measured in twenty-foot equivalent units, in two phases of about 1.1 and 0.9 million units.
The private partner designs, builds, finances and operates the terminal for a fixed period, then hands it back.
A major port at Ennore, near Chennai; it is run as a company, unlike most major ports, which are run by port authorities.
More berths and deeper drafts let larger ships call at the port and lower the cost of moving goods.

ul: **Why it matters:** port capacity lowers logistics costs and supports manufacturing and exports.

prel.d: Twenty-foot equivalent unit, the standard measure of container capacity.
A public–private partnership model of design, build, finance, operate and transfer.

qs.q: Examine the role of port capacity expansion and public–private partnerships in improving logistics in India.

topics.t: Region-specific antivenom for pit viper bites in the North East
topics.news: Researchers at the Institute of Advanced Study in Science and Technology, Guwahati, developed a bivalent antivenom against the venoms of two pit vipers of the North East, the red-tailed bamboo pit viper and Pope’s pit viper. In laboratory tests it neutralised the venom better than the polyvalent antivenom now used across India. The results are from laboratory and animal studies; it is not yet in clinical use.

rows: Made against the ‘Big Four’ snakes: Indian cobra, common krait, Russell’s viper and saw-scaled viper.
Venom varies by species and region, so the national product binds poorly to the venoms of several North-East pit vipers.
Made from the venoms of two species, so it can be matched to the snakes of a region.
A viper with a heat-sensing pit between the eye and nostril that helps it detect warm-blooded prey.

ul: **Next steps:** clinical trials, regulatory approval and large-scale production before use in hospitals.
**Policy link:** snakebite envenoming is listed among neglected tropical diseases.

prel.d: Antibodies, usually raised in animals, that neutralise snake venom.
Effective against venoms of more than one species.
Effective against venoms of two species.

qs.q: Why is region-specific antivenom needed in India? Discuss the challenges in reducing deaths from snakebite.

topics.t: Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 on the Thirukkural
topics.news: The fifth Kashi Tamil Sangamam will run from 28 November to 12 December 2026. Its theme is learning the Thirukkural, and about 1,400 participants from Tamil Nadu are expected to visit Varanasi. The Ministry of Education organises it, with IIT Madras and Banaras Hindu University as the implementing partners.

rows: Renew the old cultural and educational links between Tamil Nadu and Kashi and promote the idea of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat.
A classical Tamil work of 1,330 couplets attributed to Thiruvalluvar, in three parts: Aram (virtue), Porul (wealth and polity) and Inbam (love).
Students, teachers, artisans, writers and others, with exhibitions and cultural events.

ul: **Language policy:** Tamil was among the first languages to be given classical status, in 2004; Marathi, Assamese, Bengali, Pali and Prakrit were added in 2024.
**Why it matters:** cultural exchange builds national integration.

prel.d: A programme that pairs States to promote cultural exchange and mutual understanding.
A status given to languages with ancient and independent literary tradition.

qs.q: How do cultural programmes such as the Kashi Tamil Sangamam strengthen national integration in a diverse country?

topics.t: Doloo greenfield airport at Silchar cleared by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs
topics.news: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved a new greenfield airport at Doloo in Silchar, Cachar district of Assam, at an estimated cost of Rs 2,014 crore. The Airports Authority of India will build it. The present Silchar airport is a civil enclave on defence land and cannot expand, which is why a separate airport is being built. The proposal had earlier been examined by the Network Planning Group under the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan.

rows: Airports Authority of India, a statutory body under the Ministry of Civil Aviation that owns and runs most civil airports.
A building of 12,351 square metres designed for about 800 passengers in peak hours.
2,705 m long and 45 m wide, Code 4C, so it can take A-320 size aircraft.
Parking for six A-320 aircraft plus a separate isolation bay for aircraft facing a security threat.
A new airport built on fresh land, as opposed to a brownfield project that expands an existing one.
A civil terminal that works inside an airbase owned by the defence forces, so civil flights depend on military clearance.

ul: **Why it matters:** Barak Valley and southern Assam depend on one constrained airport; a civil airport can help tea, agro-based trade and tourism, and improves links between the North East and the rest of India.

**Approval route:** infrastructure projects of this size are cleared by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, and PM GatiShakti checks that the site fits the roads, rail and other networks around it.

prel.d: A new airport built on a fresh site.
An aerodrome reference code showing the runway length and wingspan class an airport can handle.
A digital platform and master plan that coordinates infrastructure projects across ministries.

qs.q: Regional airports in the North East are essential for connectivity and economic integration. Examine the challenges in developing such airports and suggest measures.

topics.t: Rs 11,000 crore scheme to build a domestic construction and infrastructure equipment industry
topics.news: The Union Cabinet approved a Rs 11,000 crore scheme to strengthen the manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment in India, to be run by the Ministry of Heavy Industries over eight years from 2026-27. Manufacturers will receive incentives linked to incremental sales, and a grant of up to Rs 375 crore will help set up a dedicated testing facility. The scheme follows a Budget 2026-27 announcement.

rows: Eight years: two years (2026-27 and 2027-28) to set up facilities, five years (2028-29 to 2032-33) of incentive payment, and 2033-34 for settling the last claims.
Graded support from 13% falling to 8% of the value of incremental sales over five years, open to equipment makers and component makers.
Viability gap funding of up to Rs 375 crore for a common testing centre, so that machines can be certified in India.
Items such as ship-to-shore cranes, tunnel boring machines, hydraulic excavators and off-highway trucks.
A one-time capital grant that makes a project with high social value but weak returns financially workable.
India has the third-largest construction equipment industry in the world after China and the United States.

ul: **Why it matters:** large infrastructure programmes such as tunnels, ports and highways depend on imported machines; local production can cut import dependence and add skilled jobs.
**Design feature:** incentives are tied to incremental sales and paid after the facilities are built, so the state pays only for output that has actually been produced.

prel.d: Sales above a base-year level, used to measure the growth that qualifies for an incentive.
A capital grant to bridge the gap between a project's cost and its commercial returns.
A machine that digs tunnels through soil or rock with a rotating cutting head.

qs.q: Production-linked and sales-linked incentive schemes are used to build domestic manufacturing. Evaluate their effectiveness with reference to the capital goods sector.

topics.t: Postal Operations and Estates Management schemes continued for the 16th Finance Commission cycle
topics.news: The Cabinet approved the continuation of two Central Sector Schemes of the Department of Posts for 2026-27 to 2030-31: the Postal Operations Scheme with Rs 1,141 crore and the Estates Management Scheme with Rs 1,491 crore, together Rs 2,632 crore. India Post has about 1.65 lakh post offices, of which 1,49,655 are in rural areas.

rows: Six parts: rural access Rs 120 crore, mail network Rs 575 crore, parcel network Rs 278 crore, international mail Rs 8 crore, marketing and service quality Rs 100 crore, philately Rs 60 crore.
Builds, rebuilds, renovates and brands post offices and staff colonies, and preserves heritage postal buildings.
190 new post office buildings, 50 reconstructed, 2,550 sub-post offices renovated, 2,500 rented offices upgraded, 20 heritage buildings preserved and 150 colonies renovated.
A scheme fully funded and run by the Union Government, unlike a Centrally Sponsored Scheme where States share the cost.
The collection and study of postage stamps; the department issues commemorative stamps.
The five-year period for which the Finance Commission recommends fund sharing; the 16th cycle runs 2026-27 to 2030-31.

ul: **Why it matters:** the postal network is the widest delivery system in India and carries savings, insurance, payments and Aadhaar services to villages.
**Link to logistics:** better mail and parcel hubs help e-commerce and small sellers reach distant customers.

prel.d: A scheme funded wholly by the Union Government.
Study and collection of stamps and related postal items.
A post-office centre that helps small exporters and artisans send goods abroad.

qs.q: Despite the spread of digital communication, India Post remains important for inclusive development. Discuss its changing role.

topics.t: Cabinet approves a memorandum with Singapore on aviation maintenance, repair and overhaul
topics.news: The Union Cabinet approved the signing of a memorandum of understanding between India and Singapore for cooperation in skills and industry development in aviation maintenance, repair and overhaul, called MRO. It covers an industry-linked curriculum for aircraft maintenance engineers, exchange of expertise, internships, and partnerships to set up more MRO facilities in India.

rows: Maintenance, repair and overhaul: the inspection, servicing and rebuilding of aircraft, engines and parts.
A licensed technician who certifies that an aircraft is fit to fly.
Curriculum design, building the capacity of Indian institutes, internships with Singapore-based firms and industry partnerships.
Maintenance done abroad raises costs and keeps aircraft grounded longer, and India needs more trained engineers as fleets grow.
The aim is to make India a regional aviation workshop in line with Atmanirbhar Bharat.
Many international memoranda are placed before the Cabinet for approval before signing.

ul: **Why it matters:** MRO is a high-value service that can keep foreign exchange in the country and create skilled jobs.
**Wider ties:** India and Singapore already cooperate in skills, digital and investment partnerships.

prel.d: Maintenance, repair and overhaul of aircraft.
A non-binding document recording the intentions and plans of the parties.

qs.q: India aims to become a global hub for aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul. Discuss the opportunities and the policy gaps.

topics.t: IORA senior officials meet in New Delhi before the Council of Ministers
topics.news: The 29th meeting of the Committee of Senior Officials of the Indian Ocean Rim Association was held in New Delhi on 25 and 26 November, ahead of the 25th Council of Ministers meeting on 27 November. India chairs the association for 2025-27 under the theme of innovation, openness, resilience and adaptability, and links its chairship to the MAHASAGAR vision.

rows: An intergovernmental body of 23 member states and 12 dialogue partners working on maritime safety, trade, fisheries, the blue economy and disaster risk management.
The body that reviews how ministerial decisions are carried out and coordinates the work programmes.
The ministerial body of the association, which takes the final decisions and approves the plans prepared by the senior officials.
India's maritime vision for an open, inclusive and rules-based order in the Indian Ocean.
India holds the chair for 2025-27, the period for which it sets the agenda.

ul: **Why it matters:** about 90 per cent of India's trade by volume moves by sea, and IORA is a forum where India can shape rules on maritime security and the blue economy.
**Reading tip:** link IORA with SAGAR, MAHASAGAR, the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative and the Colombo Security Conclave.

prel.d: The Indian Ocean Rim Association, formed in 1997, with its secretariat in Mauritius.
Use of ocean resources for growth while keeping marine ecosystems healthy.
India's vision for maritime security and growth for all in the region.

qs.q: The Indian Ocean Rim Association offers India a platform to lead regional maritime cooperation. Examine its significance and limitations.

topics.t: Supreme Court declines interim bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam and sends the matter to a three-judge bench
topics.news: A Supreme Court bench headed by the Chief Justice of India declined to grant interim bail for now to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the case on the alleged conspiracy behind the 2020 north-east Delhi riots, which is under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. The court issued notice to the Delhi Police and directed that the matter go to the Chief Justice for a three-judge bench to be formed.

rows: The accused challenged a Delhi High Court order that had refused them regular bail in a conspiracy case under the anti-terror law.
Interim bail refused at present; notice issued to the police, who will be heard before interim bail is considered.
The Chief Justice, as master of the roster, will constitute a three-judge bench on the administrative side.
Section 43D(5) bars bail if the court finds the accusations prima facie true, making bail harder than under ordinary criminal law.
Temporary release while the main bail application is still pending.

ul: **Why it matters:** the case raises the balance between personal liberty under Article 21 and the state's powers under special security laws, and the length of pre-trial detention.
**Constitutional link:** the Supreme Court has said that prolonged incarceration can be a ground for bail even under strict statutes, though each case turns on its facts.

prel.d: India's main anti-terror law, first enacted in 1967 and amended several times.
The Chief Justice's power to decide which judges hear which cases.
The right to life and personal liberty.

qs.q: Special security laws often restrict the grant of bail. Discuss how the judiciary balances individual liberty and national security.

topics.t: Nepal begins the process to declare 213 missing Indians dead after the August floods
topics.news: Nepal has started the process of declaring 213 Indian nationals, who went missing in the flash floods of 26 August 2026 in the Trishuli-Bhote Koshi river system, as presumed dead. Nepal's disaster management authority has published the list of names. The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu has asked families to send objections or corrections by 2 December 2026, after which Nepal will finalise the list and issue the declaration so that death certificates can be obtained.

rows: Flash floods on 26 August 2026 in the Trishuli-Bhote Koshi river system.
Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority published the names and invited objections.
Families to send objections, additions or amendments to the Indian Embassy by 2 December 2026.
Nepal finalises the list and issues the formal declaration; the Embassy then seeks death certificates from local authorities.
A legal declaration that a person who has been missing for a long time or in a disaster is treated as dead, so that families can claim rights and compensation.

ul: **Why it matters:** a death certificate lets families settle insurance, property and pension claims.
**Wider lesson:** Himalayan rivers cross borders, so flood warnings and data sharing between India, Nepal and China matter for lives downstream.

prel.d: A sudden and fast rise in water level, often after cloudburst or glacial lake outburst.
A legal finding that a missing person is dead.

qs.q: Trans-boundary Himalayan floods call for regional cooperation. Discuss the issues and the role of India in disaster diplomacy in South Asia.

topics.t: Drone attack on a Riyadh financial-district tower injures two Indians; India condemns it
topics.news: A drone attack hit a tower in the Riyadh financial district that houses the Public Investment Fund. Saudi civil defence put the injured at 11, including two Indian nationals, and it was the second attack on the site within a week. India's Ministry of External Affairs condemned the attack and the Indian mission said it is helping the injured and their families. Saudi Arabia and the Houthis also exchanged warnings over Red Sea ports.

rows: A previous attack on the same site took place on 19 November.
The Saudi-led coalition warned of strikes on Hodeidah port in Yemen; the Houthis threatened Jeddah and other Saudi ports on the Red Sea.
Condemnation of the attack and consular help for the injured.
Millions of Indians live and work in the Gulf; the Gulf is also a major source of oil and remittances.

ul: **Why it matters:** attacks on Gulf cities and Red Sea ports threaten shipping, oil prices and the safety of the Indian community.
**Policy link:** the Link West policy, oil imports and the Bab-el-Mandeb route all carry exposure.

prel.d: An armed movement that controls much of northern Yemen.
A major Red Sea port of Yemen.
The sovereign wealth fund of Saudi Arabia.

qs.q: Instability in West Asia has direct economic and security consequences for India. Examine the impact on energy, trade and the diaspora.

topics.t: RBI Bulletin for November: imported inflation, NBFC credit and US policy spillovers
topics.news: The Reserve Bank's November Bulletin was released on 25 November. One article finds that imported items form 8.5% of the new consumer price index basket (base 2024=100) but accounted for about 18% of headline inflation in October 2026. Another review finds that non-banking finance companies kept double-digit credit growth and improved asset quality at the end of March 2026, helped by gold-backed retail lending.

rows: Price rise that comes from imported goods, mainly food, fuel and precious metals.
Imported items have a weight of 8.5% in the CPI basket but contributed about 18% of October inflation.
Credit grew at double digits and asset quality improved; gold-backed loans drove retail growth.
Tighter US policy news is linked to a weaker rupee, higher 10-year yields and lower Sensex returns.
The revised index uses 2024 as the base (2024=100).

ul: **Why it matters:** if import-driven shocks matter more than their weight suggests, interest rates alone cannot control inflation.
**Note for answers:** the views in these Bulletin articles are the authors' own and not the Reserve Bank's official position.

prel.d: Non-banking financial company: a lender that does not hold a banking licence.
The reference year against which price changes are measured.
A method that measures how a variable moves around the date of a news event.

qs.q: Imported inflation limits the effectiveness of domestic monetary policy. Discuss with reference to recent price trends.

topics.t: International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women and the 16 Days campaign
topics.news: The International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women is observed on 25 November and starts the 16 Days of Activism that end on 10 December. The 2026 theme is to ensure justice, protect survivors and end impunity. New UN data from 54 countries show that only about 1 in 4 women who face violence seek any help and just 7% go to the police.

rows: 25 November each year, set by the United Nations General Assembly in 1999; the date recalls the Mirabal sisters of the Dominican Republic, murdered in 1960.
A campaign from 25 November to 10 December, Human Rights Day.
About one in three women and girls, around 840 million, have faced physical or sexual violence.
About 23% seek help from anyone, 7% report to the police; in Asia the help-seeking figure is 16%.
Between 63% and 97% of reported cases worldwide end without a conviction.
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005, the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act 2013 and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita offences.

ul: **Why it matters:** low reporting hides the true scale of violence and weakens access to justice.
**Link to SDGs:** Goal 5 on gender equality includes ending all forms of violence against women and girls.

prel.d: Freedom from punishment for those who commit an offence.
The killing of women and girls because of their gender.
The sustainable development goal on gender equality and empowerment of women.

qs.q: Despite strong laws, violence against women persists in India. Examine the gaps in access to justice and suggest reforms.
